newsitem.title: UK: Sean Connery ad gives Scottish nationalists boost.
newsitem.headline: Sean Connery ad gives Scottish nationalists boost.

text.p: A political broadcast by film star Sean Connery for the Scottish Nationalists gave the party a record membership boost, a spokeswoman said on Saturday.

Almost 600 people applied to join the Scottish National Party (SNP), which has said an independent Scotland would be the world's 21st richest nation, after the Scottish star made a television appeal for the party on Thursday night.
The party hopes he can make more broadcasts in the run up to the general election, due by next May, she said.

In his broadcast, Connery welcomed the recent return to Scotland of the highly symbolic Stone of Destiny which was taken to England 700 years ago by Edward I. But he said: "We need the substance, not just the symbols. We need more."
The main target for the Scottish Nationalists is the opposition Labour Party, the biggest party in Scotland and well ahead of the ruling Conservatives in British opinion polls.

The nationalists enjoy nearly 30 percent support in Scotland while Labour stands at 48 percent and the Conservatives are running third with about 15 percent. Labour has been severely damaged in Scotland by a series of policy switches on its plans for a referendum on a devolved Scottish parliament.

Since 1296, the Stone of Destiny had been under a throne in London's Westminster Abbey, where England's kings and queens have traditionally been crowned. It has now being taken to the Scottish capital of Edinburgh.
